description.narrative:
Sida kommer att bidra till implementeringen av ett forskningsprogram 2019-2021. Forskningsorganisationen har som målsättning att påverka policys och verksamhet i Afghanistan och bidra till ökad kunskap genom att producera god forskning för att stimulera en forsknings- och lärandekultur där faktabaserade analyser efterfrågas. Organisationen har identifierat följande breda teman som fokus för sin forskning de kommande tre åren: management av naturresurser, samhällsstyrning och politisk ekonomi, sociala skyddsnät, gender, migration och regionalt samarbete och konstitutionella lagar. Dessa teman ligger i linje med organisationens existerande kapacitet och komparativa fördelar och relaterar också till afghanska prioriteringar. Organisationen är också relevant för den övergripande målsättningen för det svenska samarbetet att bidra till en demokratisk, fredlig och hållbar utveckling med långsiktig ekonomisk tillväxt som kommer människor som lever i fattigdom till del och för flera av samarbetsstrategins mer specifika delmål. Forskningen bedrivs av både afghanska och internationella forskare. Organisationen kommer att fortsätta att stärka sin institutionella kapacitet och förmågan att nu ut med sin forskning samt utbilda och stödja kvinnliga och manliga afghanska forskare.
Organisationen har följande övergripande mål för den kommande treårsperioden: - stimulera beslutsfattande baserat på fakta - ytterligare förbättra kvalitén på organisationens forskning - förbättra organisationens strategier och produkter för att sprida och kommunicera sin forskning - utveckla och underhålla institutionella samarbeten och relevanta partnerskap - säkerställa kvalitén i interna styrning och administration - utveckla en strategi för att säkerställa organisatorisk effektivitet - stärka personal i deras kompetens och kapacitet.
Sidas stöd till organisationen är cirka 5 MSEK per år.

Sida will contribute to the implementation of the Research organisation's Strategic Plan 2019-2021. The research organisation aims to inform policy and practice and produce knowledge by conducting high quality research to nurture a culture of research and learning in Afghanistan and stimulate demand for evidenced-based research. The organisation has identified the following six broad research areas as focus for the coming three years: Natural Resource Management, Governance and Political Economy, Social Protection, Gender, Migration & Regional Cooperation and Constitutional Law. These thematic research areas are aligned with existing strengths and research capacity and also match the policy priorities identified in the Afghanistan Peace and Development Framework (ANPDF) from 2016. The research is also relevant to the overarching objective of Sweden’s cooperation with Afghanistan to contribute to democratic, peaceful and sustainable development, and long-term economic growth that benefits people living in poverty, and to several the cooperation strategy’s more specific objectives. The research will be conducted by both international and Afghan researchers. Apart from producing and disseminating research, the organisation will also strengthen its institutional capacity and train and support Afghan female and male researchers.
The organisation identifies the following overarching objectives for its activities the coming three years: - Nurture evidence-based decision-making. - Strengthening the quality and scope of the research. - Strengthen communication and dissemination strategies and products. - Develop and sustain mutually-beneficial partnerships. - Ensure quality internal management and administration processes. - Develop a strategy for ensuring organisational effectiveness. - Strengthen the human resource capacity and representation of staff.
Sida's support to the organisation is approx. 5 MSEK annually.

The overall intended outcome of the programme is to provide solid, evidence-based research, conducted with the highest ethical and quality-controlled standards, to stimulate public discourse and policy decisions that are rooted in the reality of Afghanistan. The focus of the research is mainly on Humanitarian assistance, Natural Resource Management, Economic Development and Social protection and livelihoods.
Furthermore, AREU aims to ensure the early by-in of the research and to pave the way for better cooperation and uptake of the research. This has entailed a multi-pronged outreach approach targeting international community and civil society organisations, as well as influential thinkers and public intellectuals within and outside the country, and in the end the Afghan people. AREU has the following specific objectives for its extended Strategic Plan 2019-2021:
- Nurture evidence-based decision-making. - Strengthening the quality and scope of AREUs research. - Strengthen AREUs communication and dissemination strategies and products. - Develop and sustain mutually-beneficial partnerships. - Ensure quality internal management and administration processes within AREU. - Develop a strategy for ensuring organisational effectiveness. - Strengthen the human resource capacity and representation of AREU staff. - Strengthening the quality of research and dissemination of findings.

In 2019, AREU published 32 publications (11 English, 10 Dari and 10 Pashto) representing each of six themes 8 publications under Natural Resources Management 6 publications under Gender 4 publications under Governance and Political Economy 6 publications under Social Protection and Livelihood 6 publications under Constitutional and Legal Studies Research, and 1 publication under Migration and Regional Cooperation.
AREU established relationships and delivered its evidence based research to between 710 policy makers under each of its research themes in 2019 and conducted a number of briefings, consultations and presentation to inform and influence Afghan and international stakeholders.
In 2019 and 2020 AREU was defined as the top think tank in Afghanistan by the Lauder institute of the University of Pennsylvania and rose from fifth in Central Asia in 2018 to third. In 2019 and 2020 AREU issued 69 publications in all three languages. AREU also signed a number of MoUs with Afghan and International Institutions, including World Economic Forum and Columbia International Affairs Online.
In 2020 AREU published all together 37 papers, 16 English, 11 Dari and 10 Pashtu publications. the breakdown of the publications per thematic area is: Natural Resource Management: English (6), Dari (6) and Pashtu (6). Gender: English (3), Dari (3) and Pashtu (3). The fourth paper prepared Governance and Political Economy: English (3), Dari (3) and Pashtu (3)Constitutional and Legal Studies Research: 1 paper Social protection and Livelihoods: English (1) Regional Cooperation and migration studies: 1 Paper
In 2021, AREU published a total of 23 papers. The breakdown is: 9 English, 7 Dari and 7 Pashto. The breakdown of the publications per thematic area is: Gender: English (2), Dari (2), Pashto (2) Governance and Political Economy: English (7), Dari (4), Pashto (4) Natural Resources Management: Dari (1), Pashto (1)
AREU translated 11 Years of the Elimination of Violence Against Women (EVAW) Law: A Literature Review of the Implementation of the EVAW Law (2009-2020) into Dari and Pashto but did not upload/publish this version of the paper due to the political sensitivities.In addition, AREU managed to distribute Dari and Pashto publications across south and south eastern provinces in partnership with PenPath volunteers coauthorship of all team members in Kabul in different AREU publications a record level of visits to the AREU website at the peak of changes in August 2021.
AREU published a total of 5 publications in 2022. Their breakdown is: 11 English, 10 Dari and 10 Pashto publications. The breakdown of the publications per theme are as follows: Governance and Political Economy: English (2) | Dari (2) | Pashto (2) Social Protection & Livelihoods: English (4) Dari (4) Pashto 4)
AREU engaged Afghan policymakers throughout the life cycle of each project through briefings, consultations, as well as private briefings. In 2022, AREU was approached by at least 6 institutions to help with the development of research tools and methodologies. Examples include the American University in Afghanistan, Kateb University, The Asia Foundation, several civil society groups, healthcare institutions, government and international organizations.
In 2023, only two research studies were completed.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
